title.narrative: Solomon Islands Roads and Aviation Project

description.narrative: Improve operational safety and oversight of air transport and associated infrastructure, strengthen the sustainability and climate resilience of the Project Roads, and in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to provide an immediate response to the Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

The development objective of the Roads and Aviation Project for Solomon Islands is to improve operational safety and oversight of air transport and associated infrastructure, strengthen the sustainability and climate resilience of the project roads, and in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency, to provide an immediate response to the eligible crisis or emergency.it has four components.The first component, Honiara and munda airports infrastructure investments is to improve operational safety and overall infrastructure resilience to climate change at Honiara, this activity will include: (i) 5 cm overlay of existing runway (including pavement strength testing and drainage improvements); (ii) installation of airfield ground lighting for runway (AGL); (iii) construction of rescue fire service (RFS) vehicle station; (iv) installation of automatic weather observation system (AWOS); (v) installation of very small aperture terminal (VSAT) communications systems; (vi) installation of automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast (ADS-b) ground stations and aircraft equipage; and, (vii) provision of equipment for improved power supply; second component, Malaita road improvement and maintenance program aim to improve the climate resilience of the malaita road network through a combination of specific spot improvements and overall system condition strengthening via adaptive maintenance measures; third component, institutional strengthening includes: (i) training needs analysis; (ii) airport operational training; (iii) airport regulatory training; (iv) preparation of a strategic plan for the sustainability of solomon airlines (i.e., airline strategy review); (v) airport master planning studies for both honiara and munda airports; (vi) preparation of an aviation sector strategy; (vii) technical support to civil aviation authority of solomon islands (CAASI) to improve safety and security oversight; and, (viii) technical support so solomon islands airport corporation limited (SIACL) for strengthening capabilities for airport management and operation; and fourth component, project implementation support will be located in ministry of communications and aviation (MCA), providing support to both mca and ministry of infrastructure development (MID) for project preparation and implementation. in addition, the existing PAIP technical and fiduciary services unit (TFSU) will provide support to the pst for procurement, financial management, safeguards, contract management, monitoring and evaluation, audit, communications subscription for vsat, and technical guidance, particularly for aviation matters.

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Operations Manual. (Section I.C of Schedule 2 tothe Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with the Annual Work Plans and Budgets approved by theAssociation for the respective fiscal year, and inform the Association prior to making or allowing to be made any change to theAnnual Work Plans and Budgets. (Section I.D of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall maintain until the Closing Date, a Project Support Team comprised of, inter alia: (i) a program manager; (ii) aproject manager; (iii) a deputy project manager; (iv) a finance manager; (v) a procurement specialist; (vi) a national safeguardsspecialist; (vii) a community liaison officer; and (viii) a project accountant.(Section I.A.4 of Schedule 2 to the FinancingAgreement)

The Recipient shall maintain, in collaboration with the Program Countries, until the Closing Date, a Program Steering Committee,with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association. (Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)
The Recipient shall maintain, until December 31, 2019, a Service Agreement with TAL, with terms and conditions satisfactory to theAssociation. (Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall maintain, until the Closing Date, a focal point within the Ministry of Communication and Aviation, with termsof reference, qualificaitons and experience satisfactory to the Association. (Section I.A.5 of Schedule 2 to the FinancingAgreement)The Recipient shall maintain, until the Closing Date, a focal point within the Ministry of Infrastructure Development,with terms of reference, qualificaitons and experience satisfactory to the Association. (Section I.A.6 of Schedule 2 to theFinancing Agreement)

The Recipient shall, in collaboration with the other Program Countries, ensure that the Regional Procurement Evaluation Committee,is maintained throughout the Project implementation period, comprised of representatives the Program Countries and PASO to beresponsible for evaluating regional level procurement activities under the Project. (Section I.A.3 of Schedule 2 to the FinancingAgreement)

To ensure proper oversight of the Project at the national level, the Recipient shall establish, by not later than three (3) monthsafter the Effective Date (or such other date which the Association has confirmed in writing to the Recipient is reasonable andacceptable under the circumstances, as determined by the Association in its sole discretion) and maintain until the Closing Date, aNational Steering Committee with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association. (Section I.A.2 of Schedule 2to the Financing Agreement)

title.narrative: Number of person days worked by women in routine maintenance activities (person-days)

comment.narrative: Target not achieved (14 percent). Out of 169 people employed in the two routine maintenance works, 12 people were female (=7.1 percent). title.narrative: Grievances responded and/or resolved within the stipulated service standards

comment.narrative: Target exceeded (133 percent). The project's grievance redress mechanism (GRM) defined service standards for responding to and ideally resolving complaints (High/Med/Low priority 5/10/30 working days respectively). With the closure of two complaints received during the fourth quarter of 2024, all the 56 complaints received during project implementation were responded and/or resolved within the stipulated service standards by the project's closing date.

title.narrative: Number of training courses related to GBV delivered

comment.narrative: Target exceeded (260 percent). The GBV consultant successfully completed all deliverables under their contract. This included four trainings to the service providers in Honiara, Munda, and Malaita; four awareness sessions for the contractors engaged under SIRAP; and five community awareness sessions at Munda and Malaita project sites. A total of 13 training/awareness sessions was delivered by the GBV consultant from 2020 to 2023.

title.narrative: People with enhanced access to transportation services (CRI)

comment.narrative:
Target fully achieved (100 percent). For aviation, the opening of the new terminal building and the upgraded runway, taxiway, and apron at Munda Airport on October 10, 2023 led to the resumption of Solomon Islands direct flights from Brisbane to Munda on January 6, 2024. The actual value reached the end target of 721,000, or the entire population of Solomon Islands as the upgraded infrastructure became in use as an international airport. For roads, upgrading of Koa, Bio1, and Bio2 Bridges was completed on September 24, 2024. Routine maintenance and regravelling of 17 km of Malaita North Road was completed on August 9, 2024, and that of 21 km of Malaita East Road was completed on November 8, 2024. The actual value reached the end target of 82,000, or those living in the 12 wards connected by the Malaita North and East Roads.
This corporate results indicator (CRI) was added to SIRAP at the restructuring in August 2023 to meet the CRI requirements.

title.narrative: Availability of social services within an accessible distance

comment.narrative: Target exceeded (113 percent). This measured the number and type of organizations in a community that provided social welfare-based services, including counselling, case management, and safe shelter. In Munda, there were two social service providers; however, both did not provide a safe shelter. In Malaita, there were five service providers and out of the five, one provided a safe shelter. All the services providers were not based in the communities. They were all based in the Provincial Headquarters, and they deployed to communities whenever there was a case. It should be noted that SIRAP had no direct or indirect influence on this indicator.

title.narrative: Equipment and systems standardized with regional standards

comment.narrative:
Target fully achieved (100 percent) against the revised target or substantially achieved (80 percent) against the original target. ADS-B ground stations and VSAT communications systems at Honiara and Munda Airports were completed and commissioned under SIRAP. While ADS-B ground station at Munda Airport became inoperable during Q3 2023, this was repaired on May 27, 2024. The VSAT communications systems at Honiara and Munda Airports were commissioned in September 2022 and had additional filters installed in March 2023.
The end target was revised from 5 to 4 at the restructuring in August 2023 as ADS-B aircraft equipage could not be procured after four attempts and was not implemented under SIRAP.

The end target of 80 percent was not achieved due to amendments to bid/proposal closing dates.

The target was revised at the restructuring in August 2023 to reflect the reduction of gravel road length to be maintained from 210 km to 38 km, and the reduction in routine maintenance contract duration from four years to six months.

title.narrative: Implementation of recommended PASO annual work plan

It should be noted that the actual value was 0 percent in 2019, 30 percent in 2020 and 2021, 59 percent in 2022 and 2023, and 100 percent in 2024.

title.narrative: Identified climate resilient investments constructed and in use

comment.narrative:
Target exceeded both against the revised target (113 percent) and the original target (180 percent). Climate Resilient investments originally included concreting 5 steep grade sections of gravel roads, which subsequently increased to 6 sections (with a total length of 1,300 m, consisting of CH 8.170-CH8.370 on North Road, and CH4.000-CH4.160, CH7.180–CH7.320, CH12.750-CH12.950, CH13.050-CH13.350, and CH16.700-CH17.000 on East Road) and 3 bridges (Koa, Bio1, and Bio2 Bridges) replacements. The completion date for the three bridges was September 24, 2024, for Malaita North Road was August 9, 2024, and for East Road was November 8, 2024.
The end target was from 5 to 8 at the restructuring in August 2023.

The end target was revised from 50% to 19% to reflect the reduced scope of works from 210 km to 38 km at the restructuring in August 2023.

title.narrative: People with enhanced access to transportation services

comment.narrative: The opening of the new terminal building and the upgraded runway, taxiway, and apron on October 10, 2023 led to the resumption of Solomon Islands direct flights from Brisbane to Munda on January 6, 2024. The actual value has been updated to the end target of 721,000, or the entire population of Solomon Islands as the upgraded infrastructure is now in use as an international airport and as an alternative airport to Honiara.

title.narrative: Identified climate resilient investments constructed and in use

comment.narrative: Climate Resilient investments originally included concreting five steep grade sections of gravel roads, which subsequently increased to six sections (with a total length of 1,300 m, consisting of CH 8.170-CH8.370 on North Road, and CH4.000-CH4.160, CH7.180–CH7.320, CH12.750-CH12.950, CH13.050-CH13.350, and CH16.700-CH17.000 on East Road) and three bridges (Koa, Bio1, and Bio2 Bridges) replacements. Five steep graded concrete sections (CH 8.170-CH8.370 on North Road, and CH4.000-CH4.160, CH7.180–CH7.320, CH12.750-CH12.950, and CH16.700-CH17.000 on East Road) and Koa, Bio1, and Bio2 Bridges are 100 percent completed, which account for the Actual (Current) value of 8. The end value is expected to reach 9 once the remaining graded section at CH13.050-CH13.350 is completed.

title.narrative: Availability of social services within an accessible distance

comment.narrative: The number and type of organizations in a community that provide social welfare-based services, including counselling, case management, and safe shelter. In Munda, there are two social service providers; however, both do not provide a safe shelter. In Malaita, there are five service providers and out of the five, one provides a safe shelter. All the services providers are not based in the communities. They are all based in the Provincial Headquarters, and they deploy to communities whenever there is a case. It should be noted that SIRAP has no direct or indirect influence on this indicator.

title.narrative: Airport Certification according to ICAO safety and security standards at Munda Airport

comment.narrative: The interim Airport Operating Certificate (Part 139) issued by CAASI on February 28, 2024 was extended to November 30, 2024. Following SIACL's submission of the required operating manuals to CAASI, the Pacific Aviation Safety Office (PASO) undertook the certification audits in October 2024, and CAASI noted their plan of issuing the full certificate on December 1, 2024 for 24 months. The end target is achievable within Q4 2024.

title.narrative: Airport Certification according to ICAO safety and security standards at Munda Airport

comment.narrative: The interim Airport Operating Certificate (Part 139) issued by CAASI on February 28, 2024 was up to May 31, 2024. In mid-May 2024, SIACL submitted a letter to CAASI to extend the current interim arrangement by another six month. With technical assistance from PASO, SIACL continues to work through updating airport manuals, processes, and plans to comply with ICAO requirements and CAASI oversight.

title.narrative: Percentage of women in the community advisory committees established for routine maintenance and regravelling works in Malaita

comment.narrative:
Target exceeded (106 percent). This measured the percentage of women in the community advisory committees (CAC) established for routine maintenance and regravelling works for 17 km of North and 21 km of East Roads in Malaita. The four CACs had a total of 47 members, of which 10 members were represented by women.
This indicator was added to SIRAP at the restructuring in August 2023 to replace the original indicator 'Number of person days worked by women in routine maintenance activities'.
